title: The Hallway Light
hook: My dad had one rule: the hallway light stays on all night. If it's ever off... don't get out of bed.
lines: When I was nine, my dad had one rule for our house.
The hallway light stays on all night. Always.
And if you ever wake up and it's off... don't get out of bed. Don't call for us. Just wait for morning.
I thought he was scared of burglars.
Then, one night in December, I woke up... and the crack under my door was black.
Somewhere out in the dark hall, I heard my mom's voice. Honey? The power's out. Come here, I've got a flashlight.
But there was no flashlight beam. Not under the door. Not anywhere.
So I pulled the blanket over my head... and I didn't answer.
The voice came closer. Right outside my door. It's okay, sweetheart. It's just me.
It kept saying that... over and over... until the sun came up.
At breakfast, Mom swore she'd slept straight through the night.
Dad didn't say a word. He just got the stepladder from the garage, climbed all the way up, and screwed the bulb back in.
Our ceilings are ten feet high. Whatever loosened that bulb... didn't need a ladder.
